deep.reconstruction:
Setting: small k-linear (k-additive) categories P, Q; for a k-linear category P, P^& denotes the category of k-linear presheaves P° → Ab_k (Ab_k = k-modules), i.e. the free k-linear cocompletion of P. Hom_{k!} denotes the cocontinuous (colimit-preserving) k-linear functors, and Bil_{k!!} the k-bilinear functors that are cocontinuous in each variable. Dually, Hom^{!} and Bil^{!!} refer to limit-preserving functors and P^{&°} to the free completion.

(1) Dém. This proves that (P⊗_k Q)^& is the tensor product of P^& and Q^& in the 2-category of cocomplete k-linear categories. The chain is:
- Bil_{k!!}(P^&,Q^&;M) ≃ Hom_{k!}(P^&, Hom_{k!}(Q^&,M)).
- By the universal property of free cocompletion, Hom_{k!}(Q^&,M) ≃ Hom_k(Q,M).
- Hence the whole is ≃ Hom_k(P, Hom_k(Q,M)).
- By currying for the k-linear tensor product of categories, this is ≃ Hom_k(P⊗_kQ, M).
- By free cocompletion again, this is ≃ Hom_{k!}((P⊗_kQ)^&, M).
The dual statement is that (P⊗Q)^{&°} represents bi-continuous bilinear functors out of P^{&°}×Q^{&°}.

(2) Appl. 3. Let M be k-linear and cocomplete. Grothendieck defines a comparison functor (*) P^&⊗_k M → Hom_k(P°,M) =: P^&_M, the M-valued presheaves on P. On elementary tensors it sends L⊗x to x̃∘L, where x̃: Ab_k → M is the unique cocontinuous functor with k ↦ x, i.e. V ↦ V⊗x. This uses Hom_{k!}(Ab_k,M) ≃ M, since Ab_k = (one-object category k)^&.

He claims (*) is fully faithful and sketches a proof:
- Embed M into M^& by Yoneda, which is fully faithful. He notes in the margin that this requires a larger universe.
- Hence Hom_k(P°,M) → Hom_k(P°,M^&) is fully faithful.
- Hom_k(P°,M^&) ≃ Bil_k(P°×M°, Ab_k) ≃ (P⊗M)^&, which by part (1) is ≃ P^&⊗M^&.
- M^& is again cocomplete.
The remaining step, marked 'pl. fid ?', is whether P^&⊗M → P^&⊗M^& (or the canonical map to Bil_k(P^&×M°,Ab_k)) is fully faithful.

The intended (true) result is the standard equivalence P^& ⊠ M ≃ [P°,M] for cocomplete M. Overall this is a lemma in a 'linearization/abelianization' program for k-linear cocomplete categories.
errors: The 'Dualement' line as transcribed has (P^& ⊗_k Q)^{&°}; it should presumably be (P⊗_kQ)^{&°}. This is a slip in the manuscript or the transcription.

The full-faithfulness sketch in Appl. 3 has a genuine gap, which Grothendieck himself flags with 'pl. fid ?'. Tensoring with P^& does not obviously preserve full faithfulness of M → M^&, so the reduction to M^& is incomplete as written.

The meaning of P^&⊗_k M is not fixed on this page: is it a universally defined tensor product of cocomplete categories, or a formal one on generators? The functor is only specified on elementary tensors L⊗x.
The line 'Hom_k(P^{&°};M^&) = Hom_k(M°;Ab_k)' is garbled. The intended identification is presumably Hom_k(P°,M^&) ≃ Hom_k(P°⊗M°, Ab_k) ≃ Hom_k(M°, P^&).
Using M^& for a large M requires a universe change. Grothendieck notes this ('un univers plus gros') but does not resolve it.

ideas.what: Free k-linear cocompletion P^& with Hom_{k!}(P^&,M) ≃ Hom_k(P,M), and Hom_{k!}(Ab_k,M) ≃ M
ideas.modern_name: Enriched free cocompletion / enriched Yoneda (Kan extension along Yoneda)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kelly (Basic Concepts of Enriched Category Theory, 1982); unenriched version in SGA4 (Grothendieck–Verdier)

ideas.what: (P⊗_kQ)^& is the tensor product of P^& and Q^& for functors cocontinuous in each variable
ideas.modern_name: Tensor product of cocomplete (locally presentable) k-linear categories; presheaf categories are multiplicative under it
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kelly 1982; Bird (thesis, 1984); later Deligne (1990), López Franco and others

ideas.modern_name: PSh(P) ⊠ M ≃ Fun(P°,M) for cocomplete M (also in Lurie HTT/HA for presentable ∞-categories)

deep.surprise_reason: These are standard facts of enriched (k-linear) cocompletion and tensor products of cocomplete categories, worked out by Kelly and Bird around the same time. The page is a private, partly incomplete derivation within the 'abelianization' notes. It is of mild historical interest, as it shows Grothendieck c.1982 working with 2-categorical tensor products of cocomplete linear categories, but it contains nothing new.
transcription_corrections: The circled page number at top is '9' (the transcription renders it as ④); bottom-left also has '9'.
The 'Dualement' formula likely reads ((P⊗_kQ)^{&°}; M) rather than ((P^&⊗_kQ)^{&°}; M).
The marginal note reads approximately 'Même chose, il faut prendre un univers plus gros', i.e. passing to M^& needs a larger universe.
'stable par lim' after M (Appl. 3) is the underlined colimit symbol lim→ ('stable par limites inductives'); likewise in 'NB M^& stable par lim→'.
